research.objective: Investigate the provided aquifer and groundwater source documents comprehensively to establish an accurate, traceable understanding of the subsurface and groundwater system at every relevant geographic and vertical scale. The ultimate goal is to produce a detailed, evidence-grounded scientific synthesis and enable an explorable representation of the region: interactive geographic maps, aquifer profiles, borehole and well views, historical groundwater charts, hydrochemical and resource layers, geological cross-sections, and three-dimensional subsurface visualizations wherever the evidence genuinely supports them. Identify and preserve the underlying observations, geometries, coordinates, depth intervals, lithological sequences, measurements, time periods, spatial variations, and relationships necessary for these outcomes. Investigate district-wide interpretations as well as meaningful differences between talukas, blocks, localities, monitoring stations, wells, and boreholes. Treat tables, maps, figures, annexures, lithologs, and primary records as potentially essential evidence rather than supplementary material to be ignored. Prioritize completeness of material evidence, scientific fidelity, provenance, and accurate spatial representation over minimizing the number of pages selected. Exercise judgment to avoid redundant work, but never discard distinct observations merely because they appear in similarly structured pages. Separate directly observed facts from report interpretations, derived calculations, and hypothetical visual approximations; explicitly document what cannot be established or visualized reliably from the available sources.
research.domain_context: Aquifer mapping, hydrogeology, groundwater resources, groundwater quality, and subsurface characterization. The consumer is Subsurface India, an exploratory public-facing experience in which people investigate the evidence behind groundwater conditions and subsurface structure through explanations, maps, time-series, well and litholog profiles, cross-sections, and potentially 3D views. Sources may combine regional descriptions with taluka/block assessments, observation-well inventories, borehole logs, aquifer-disposition tables, geophysical and hydrogeological figures, and historical monitoring data. The engine itself must remain capable of planning, executing, and synthesizing research without assuming any particular report layout or fixed output schema.
research.summary: CGWB West Central Region Dec-2021 NAQUIM for Gandhinagar District (2163 sq km, 22deg56'-23deg36'N 72deg23'-73deg05'E, RL 56-126 m) documents Cambay-basin Quaternary alluvial multi-layer system thickening east (<50 m) to west (>400 m, max ~700 m) over Tertiary/Miocene, basalt and Himmatnagar Sandstone. Framework to 300-611 m is phreatic Unconfined A (0-90 m, 15-90 m thick) plus Confined I/B (55-150 m), II/C (90-210 m) and III/D (245-300 m) plus deeper E-H, separated by aquitards and Blue Clay Tertiary marker, modelled in RockWorks16 from 73 wells +23 logs into 8 sections A-H, fence and 3D. Taluka zonation deepens westward: Dahegam shallowest (0-110 m, no III) vs Gandhinagar/Kalol/Mansa to 300 m with III. Phreatic DTW 2017 9.45-72.2 m pre to 3.03-71.2 m post (Mubarak Pura deepest, Dahegam shallowest); confined decadal 2009-18 48.69-118.43 m Aq-I and 58.05-194.6 m Aq-II; 2008-17 trends mixed unconfined (rises to 3.77 m/yr near Sabarmati/Narmada vs falls to 0.93 m/yr) and near-universal confined falls to -5.03 to -5.13 m/yr at Pethapur, pump +~3 m/yr. GEC-15 Mar 2017 Over-Exploited district 113.55% (draft 53377.70 vs availability 47007.72 Ham), Dahegam 106.31%, Gandhinagar 104.02%, Kalol 114.03%, Mansa 139.35%, zero future availability; CGWA protection below 200 m. Quality generally fresh within 200 m (BIS TDS 500/2000) but confined TDS increases east-west 400-3210 (Nasmed 3210) and unconfined 350-1320, fluoride >1.5 ppm in 19 villages (Dahegam 09, Gandhinagar 06, Kalol 02, Mansa 02). Supply-side exhausted (13341.51 MCM unsaturated, 2001.22 MCM required at Sy 0.15 vs 12.17 surplus vs 41.55 committed, Nil balance); MIS on 46726 ha saving 70.09 MCM modeled to ~97.29% (Mansa remains OE 122.31%). Primary evidence: 27 unconfined +25 I +18 II station series with lat/lon/elevation, 45 May-17 TDS points, 38 exploration +35 piezometer constructions with screens to 611 m, 42 well-inventory records (Sr.1-13 DMS georeferenced, rest locality-only), ~17 lithologs (Sertha 353 m, Giyod 450.94 m, basalts 227.5-267.9 m, 118-189 m clays). Coordinates lack CRS/datum, visuals remain figure-only, inconsistencies retained, baselines dated (2017, 2008-17) not current; metric 3D requires surveyed transects and borehole ties.
limitations: Only PDF pp.1-2,7-35 examined in batch 1; full 125-page coverage requires batches 2-4 for fence/3D, disposition p42, chemistry/resource, taluka and annexures.
No lat/lon CRS/datum, surveyed well coordinates or transect endpoint coordinates in text; Fig.6-16 geometries, contours, scales not numerically extractable.
Water-level extremes station-named minima/maxima without well depths/screens; confined decadal vs single-year phreatic not directly comparable.
Table-9 only aggregated drilling ranges; well-wise details require annexures; p25 depth-discharge pairing layout-inferred.
Land-use/crop tables variant spellings, Summer mislabeled as Ravi; soil qualitative UNDP summary without map/dates.
Resource (GEC-15 Mar 2017), quality (19 villages), levels (2016-17, 2008-17) dated baselines; must not be presented as current.
Text layer pp.36-40 captions only; lithology, picks, scales, orientations, borehole controls not recoverable without image rendering.
Single Table-12 lacks per-well, per-taluka, coordinate, date, method; unconfined transmissivity '-' unexplained.
Quality maps, categorisation, feasible-area, section/fence/3D and hydrograph regressions figure-reference only at available resolution.
No CRS/datum for lat/lon, no well depths/screens in trend pages; only combined Pre&Post slopes preserved.
GEC-15 method and stage formula not stated; Table OCR drops decimals requiring verification; Mg/l presumed mg/l.
Coordinate precision mixed 2-decimal vs 5-8 decimal; clustered wells share identical X/Y without offsets.
Depth-below-ground, elevation, head semantics mixed; WL ranges lack season/date/method.
Resource figures mix ham and mcm without conversion; GWRE-2017, May-17 quality, 2008-2017 levels dated not current.
pp95-98 headers lack aquifer name, lithology, casing/screen type; ZFrom interpreted as screens but not defined.
Phreatic transmissivity missing; stratigraphy Recent to Miocene undifferentiated; aquitard thicknesses not tabulated.
Taluka visual geometries, hydrograph values, orientations/vertical exaggeration not recoverable from text.
Only Sr.1-13 grounded with full records; Sl.14-36/37-42 numeric column mapping requires header reconciliation.
No CRS/datum, ground elevation, litholog, screen, yield, quality in well-inventory chunks; Sl.16-42 no precise placement.
SWL depth below MP not elevation; head not derivable without MP elevation; W08 anomalous must be excluded.
Litholog chunks lithology and depth only; no coordinates, collar levels, dates, screens, aquifer names.
Numeric fidelity requires page images; values assumed metres; Gram Bharti truncated, Charada partial, p125 visual-only.
No georeferenced figures in litholog/inventory chunks; metric 3D not supportable from batch alone.
Do not assume metric 3D; differentiate measured intervals, source-drawn sections/fence/3D, and interpolation.
Do not assign district centroid to wells; preserve precision and flag observed vs approximate vs unresolved.
